# Independent Revision 26 Release-Correction Review

## Verdict

`fix`

Revision 26 causally closes the two Revision 25 Git-environment defects. Every lifecycle Git call is explicit, fixture initialization and blob authentication share one closed environment, and the hostile fresh-process regression executes the real fixture path. The combined criterion cannot pass, however, because the newly introduced exact-materialization path overclaims external TypeScript authority: the declared entrypoint is validated and propagated but is not bound to the `tsc` command selected by `npm run verify`.

This verdict does not claim release readiness, hosted CI, merge approval, actor authentication, or host isolation.

## Authentication

The SWECircuit package verifier reconstructed the serialized package with no diagnostics against compilation `sha256:002a7deab98a63b756e8f930cbcfd3927d64c0c262076a0ee9ccddfb29d01d45` and package `sha256:5165a7e0bf261d60e915a416c4eb0ce230a979f89dac90a95970e15afcf8cd4f`. The compilation, manifest, integration contract, and agent contract matched their exact raw file identities.

Raw byte counts and standard SHA-256 digests were independently recomputed for every declared context source. Result: `29/29` matched. No undeclared live source was used semantically.

## Candidate And Delta Integrity

The authenticated Candidate 12 receipt remains a single failed one-shot gate for commit `6f08e0a50ec6fd7fee76254ebd07995ae6f692db`: 426 tests, 425 passes, and the fixture commit failure. Its stdout, stderr, candidate source, materialization, Git context, and cleanup identities remain unchanged. The Revision 26 evidence does not rerun or reinterpret that gate as passing; copied fixture gates are repeatable lifecycle tests over different synthetic commits.

The exact source delta contains two modified files and two new fixture children. The release gate, parent, harness, verifier, package metadata, and lock data retain their declared byte identities. No production kernel, schema, compiler, or trust-policy source changed.

## Git Boundary Review

`final-lifecycle-helper.mjs:260` now rejects every `runGit` call without an explicit environment. Enumeration of all call sites found no omission. Fixture operations at lines 401-445 and 1454-1456 use the closed fixture environment. Outer source-status calls at lines 1113-1115 and 1562-1564 explicitly retain `process.env`, preserving the enclosing candidate Git context as required. Direct host Git supply inspections also pass explicit environments.

`fixtureRepositoryEnvironment` removes every case-insensitive key whose normalized name begins with `GIT_`, then reconstructs only `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT`. Fixture dates are added afterward. This closes the known routing variables, configuration tuples, `GIT_CONFIG`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, Git-reported local variables, mixed-case aliases, and unknown future `GIT_*` inputs.

`initializeFixtureGit` returns the exact environment used for `init`, configuration, `add`, `commit`, `rev-parse`, and status. `authenticateFixtureBlobs` receives that same object for `cat-file` and `ls-tree`. Copied-gate and copied-parent builders independently use the same closed boundary while adding their declared non-Git supplies.

The fresh-process child performs real fixture creation, commit, blob authentication, and tree enumeration under active hostile routing and configuration inputs. Its exact Git-key assertions avoid the Revision 25 denylist common-mode defect. The complete lifecycle separately exercises the copied gate and parents under a disposable candidate context.

## Blocking Finding: TypeScript Authority Is Declarative Only

The new test at `final-release-review-tests.mjs:767-793` creates a file containing arbitrary text, supplies it as the external TypeScript entrypoint, and calls only `resolveLifecycleTypeScriptEntrypoint`. It never executes that file. The test therefore proves path resolution, not TypeScript consumption.

The causal mismatch is in the unchanged gate behavior now relied on by the new lifecycle. `final-release-gate.mjs:552-578` validates the supplied entrypoint, but lines 555-556 construct `PATH` from `ROOT/node_modules/.bin`, independently of that entrypoint. Line 577 merely places the validated path back in `SWECIRCUIT_TYPESCRIPT_ENTRYPOINT`. No declared runtime source consumes that key, while `final-package.json` invokes bare `tsc` for build and typecheck. npm may therefore select the fixed checkout `.bin` shim or a candidate-local `.bin` entry even when a different external file was declared.

The copied fixture gate cannot reveal the mismatch because `applyFixtureVerifyException` replaces its aggregate verification with Node syntax checks, which do not invoke TypeScript. The later parent compilation uses its separately installed, candidate-private TypeScript entrypoint. Consequently, the complete lifecycle can pass while the declared external entrypoint is arbitrary and unused.

Link closure is also incomplete. `final-release-gate.mjs:64-96` rejects a final-component symbolic link but does not require `nlink === 1`, and the helper fallback at `final-lifecycle-helper.mjs:599-601` applies `realpath` before downstream validation, erasing evidence that the local path was a symbolic alias. This contrasts with the one-plain-unlinked-file requirement applied to the actual parent compiler at `final-release-review-parent.mjs:647-655`.

This is a blocking trust and test-quality defect under review points 6 and 7. It does not show that the recorded lifecycle used the wrong compiler; it shows that the evidence cannot establish which compiler was authoritative and does not close candidate-contained, linked, or conflicting command selection.

## Complete Lifecycle Assessment

Apart from the TypeScript authority defect, the new lifecycle structure is sound. It resolves exact `HEAD`, materializes Git blobs, creates a disposable candidate Git context, launches the child from the materialization, compares files, bytes, and digest after execution, checks candidate-context identity, and removes the candidate context, materialization, lifecycle root, and nested fixture root through bounded cleanup paths. External npm cache handling and the later candidate-private TypeScript build retain their existing controls.

## Review-Point Resolution

1. Package and all 29 context sources: pass.
2. Explicit Git environments and outer-versus-fixture authority: pass.
3. Closed case-insensitive inherited `GIT_*` boundary: pass.
4. Shared environment for fixture initialization and blob authentication: pass.
5. Hostile fresh-process Git regression: pass.
6. Exact materialization, candidate context, identity, and cleanup: pass except for the unproven external TypeScript supply.
7. Unique, external, unlinked TypeScript authority: fail.
8. Exact delta and omitted-call-site search: Git delta passes; the TypeScript test introduces a blocking false-positive claim.
9. Candidate 12 and Revision 25 evidence immutability: pass.
10. Overall route: `fix`.

## Required Correction

Bind the declared TypeScript entrypoint to the exact compiler process that runs. Bare npm `tsc` resolution must not be able to select a checkout-default, candidate-local, linked, or conflicting executable independently of the declared file. Record and compare its canonical path, byte digest, link count, and observed version.

Require both explicit and fallback entrypoints to be one plain, unlinked regular file with no path alias. Preserve duplicate, missing, and candidate-containment rejection.

Add regressions that use distinguishable compiler sentinels and prove the declared compiler is the one executed while a conflicting default and candidate-local `.bin` entry exist. Cover duplicate case variants, missing paths, directories, final and ancestor symlinks, hard links, and candidate-contained paths. Then repeat focused verification, the complete exact-materialization lifecycle, pre-freeze verification, and package-bound independent review.

Candidate 12 must remain retired and unchanged.

assumptions: The verified package and its 29 authenticated immutable context sources are the authoritative semantic inputs.
External host isolation and actor authentication remain host responsibilities and are not inferred from repository tests.
risks: A declared external TypeScript path can be accepted while npm executes a different checkout-default or candidate-local command.
Hard-linked or alias-resolved TypeScript paths are not closed by the current entrypoint checks.
The Git correction itself is sound, but the combined Revision 26 criterion remains blocked by the toolchain evidence defect.
followUps: Open a bounded correction that binds the declared TypeScript entrypoint to actual execution and closes link and candidate-local substitution.
Add hostile toolchain-selection regressions and repeat the exact lifecycle and independent review before freezing a successor.
Preserve Candidate 12 and Revision 25 evidence without rerunning or rewriting either.
